propositions: For a non-Anthropic-family primary, models_at_or_above() returns the entire ladder (all three Anthropic rungs) instead of the primary itself, because substring matching against Anthropic model names fails and falls through to the fallback
The escalation loop treats the returned ladder as a climb sequence, so the first escalation downgrades from the operator's configured model to claude-haiku-4-5 (smaller window, different provider)

largest_window_tokens() returns MODEL_LADDER[-1][1] (1,000,000 tokens) for an unlocated primary instead of the minimum ladder window, causing P8 under-blocking and silent truncation instead of rejection
prerequisites.py escalation path has the same defect: it calls models_at_or_above() then takes ladder[0], jumping to claude-haiku-4-5 for an unlocated primary

The fix changes models_at_or_above(unlocated_model) to return [model] and largest_window_tokens(unlocated_model) to return the ladder minimum, preserving single-criterion retry while stopping before cross-family rung climbing
